name: Opportunity
first: Longest-driving Mars rover (45.16 km); 14-year surface lifetime against a 90-sol design
description: Opportunity (MER-B) hit a planetary jackpot — its airbag-cocooned lander bounced 26 times across Meridiani Planum and rolled into a 22-m crater (Eagle) by sheer luck, surrounded by exposed bedrock a rover could read without driving. First images showed jarosite + "blueberry" hematite concretions, the strongest mineral evidence to that point of standing liquid water on early Mars. Over 14 years 47 days Opportunity traversed 45.16 km — the Mars rover marathon record — visiting Endurance, Victoria, and Endeavour craters. A planet-wide dust storm in June 2018 blocked sunlight from its solar panels; final transmission was 2018-06-10, and NASA declared end-of-mission 2019-02-13.

events.label: LAUNCH

events.label: TOUCHDOWN — INTO EAGLE CRATER
events.note: Bounced 26 times. Rolled into a 22-m crater by chance, surrounded by exposed bedrock.
